title: Termwise limit shifts agree across all K-injective tower resolutions
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ with levelwise exactness [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Fix unbounded derived localizations $Q_T,Q_A$ and the cochain shift convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\ell X=\lim_nX_n$ for termwise inverse limit. Fix any total right derived inverse-limit functor $L:D(\mathcal T)\to D(\mathcal A)$ with its derived unit $\eta_X:Q_A\ell X\to L(Q_TX)$, in the sense of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] for the additive functor $\ell$, computed as in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. A K-injective tower complex means one receiving only null-homotopic maps from acyclic tower complexes [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. No exactness of countable products is assumed.

For every quasi-isomorphism $q:X\to I$ with $I$ K-injective, there is a unique isomorphism $d_q:Q_A\ell I\xrightarrow{\sim}L(Q_TX)$ satisfying $L(Q_Tq)\circ d_q=\eta_I$. For another such resolution $q':X\to J$, there exists a homotopy equivalence $v:I\to J$ with $vq\simeq q'$. Every such $v$ satisfies $d_{q'}\circ Q_A(\ell v)=d_q$, independently of its homotopy-class representative. Here termwise limit sends a tower homotopy $H$ to the homotopy $\ell H$ characterized by its limit projections.

For every $r\in\mathbf Z$, $q[r]$ is again a K-injective resolution. Let $\lambda_{I,r}:\ell(I[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\ell I)[r]$ be the chain isomorphism identity on compatible tuples. For every tower chain map $v:I\to J$ one has $\lambda_{J,r}\circ\ell(v[r])=(\ell v)[r]\circ\lambda_{I,r}$. With the canonical $Q_A$ shift identifications, the isomorphism
$$\beta_{X,r}=d_q[r]\circ Q_A(\lambda_{I,r})\circ d_{q[r]}^{-1}:L(Q_T(X[r]))\xrightarrow{\sim}L(Q_TX)[r]$$
is independent of $q$, is natural for all derived tower morphisms, and is coherent for zero and addition of integer shifts. All assertions include K-injective resolutions without injective degree terms.

proof.text: The inverse limit of a tower of module sheaves is the sheaf of compatible tuples: compatible local sections glue uniquely coordinate by coordinate, and the transition equations hold after gluing by uniqueness. Its projections are jointly monic. For tower maps $a,b$, projection to level $n$ gives $\pi_n\ell(a+b)=(a_n+b_n)\pi_n=\pi_n(\ell a+\ell b)$, so $\ell$ is additive. Apply $\ell$ degreewise to a tower homotopy $f-g=dH+Hd$. Additivity and functoriality give $\ell f-\ell g=(\ell d)(\ell H)+(\ell H)(\ell d)$. The degree-$i$ map $\ell H^i$ is uniquely characterized by $\pi_n\ell H^i=H_n^i\pi_n$. Thus termwise limit descends to homotopy classes and takes homotopy equivalences to homotopy equivalences. The module-sheaf description is [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; this argument uses no exactness of products.

source.place: Agent elementary compatible-tuple and homotopy calculation; homotopies as in Definition 070H (definition-K-injective).

proof.text: Use the total-derived computation supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The universal pair and its unit are those of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], applied to the additive functor $\ell$ from step 1. In particular $\eta_I$ is invertible for every K-injective tower complex $I$, without a condition on its degree terms. For a resolution $q:X\to I$, localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] makes $Q_Tq$ invertible, hence so does $L$. Define $d_q=L(Q_Tq)^{-1}\eta_I$. It is an isomorphism and satisfies the required normalization; multiplying that normalization by $L(Q_Tq)^{-1}$ proves uniqueness. This is the inverse of the canonical comparison $c_q$ in the general derived-functor notation.

source.place: Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), computation on every K-injective, and Tag 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies); tower application: sites-cohomology.tex Section 0940 (section-derived-limits).

proof.text:
For resolutions $q:X\to I$ and $q':X\to J$, apply the Hom bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] with target $J$ to $Q_Tq'(Q_Tq)^{-1}$. Choose a chain representative $v:I\to J$. Its composite with $q$ and $q'$ have the same derived image, so the same bijection with source $X$ gives $vq\simeq q'$. Represent the inverse derived morphism with target $I$; injectivity of the two Hom bijections makes its composites with $v$ homotopic to the identities. Thus $v$ is a homotopy equivalence. Every comparison with $vq\simeq q'$ represents the same homotopy class. Naturality of the unit [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] gives $\eta_JQ_A(\ell v)=L(Q_Tv)\eta_I$, whence
$$d_{q'}Q_A(\ell v)=L(Q_Tq')^{-1}L(Q_Tv)\eta_I=L(Q_Tq)^{-1}\eta_I=d_q.$$
The first step shows independence from the chain representative.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), (1) implies (3), applied three times; Tag 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined), naturality of the computing unit.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], $q[r]:X[r]\to I[r]$ is again a K-injective resolution for every integer $r$. In degree $i$, both $\ell(I[r])$ and $(\ell I)[r]$ are $\lim_n I_n^{i+r}$. Both differentials are $(-1)^r\lim_n d_{I_n}^{i+r}$, by additivity of $\ell$. Therefore identity on these compatible tuples is the asserted chain isomorphism $\lambda_{I,r}$. For any tower chain map $v:I\to J$, both sides of its asserted naturality square have degree-$i$ map $\lim_n v_n^{i+r}$; hence the square commutes. Likewise $\lambda_{I,0}=1$ and, after canonical reindexing, $\lambda_{I,r+s}=\lambda_{I,r}[s]\lambda_{I[r],s}$: both sides are identity on tuples in degree $i+r+s$, with differential sign $(-1)^{r+s}=(-1)^r(-1)^s$. Localizing gives the same identities with the canonical shift identifications of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Definition 070H (definition-K-injective), translates of acyclic complexes; agent degreewise limit/shift calculation with the cochain convention.

proof.text:
Write $\Lambda_{I,r}=Q_A(\lambda_{I,r})$, using the canonical $Q_A$ shift identifications throughout. The formula in the statement is $\beta^q_{X,r}=d_q[r]\Lambda_{I,r}d_{q[r]}^{-1}$. For a second resolution $q':X\to J$ choose $v$ as in step 3 and put $E=Q_A(\ell v)$ and $E_r=Q_A(\ell(v[r]))$. They are isomorphisms by step 1. Step 3 at $q,q'$ and at $q[r],q'[r]$ says $d_q=d_{q'}E$ and $d_{q[r]}=d_{q'[r]}E_r$. Step 4 says $\Lambda_{J,r}E_r=E[r]\Lambda_{I,r}$. Substitution gives
$$\beta^q_{X,r}=d_{q'}[r]E[r]\Lambda_{I,r}E_r^{-1}d_{q'[r]}^{-1}=d_{q'}[r]\Lambda_{J,r}d_{q'[r]}^{-1}=\beta^{q'}_{X,r}.$$
Thus $\beta_{X,r}$ is resolution independent.

source.place: Agent cancellation of the comparison identities established in steps 3 and 4; based on Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective).

proof.text:
Let $h:Q_TX\to Q_TY$ be any derived morphism and choose resolutions $q:X\to I$, $p:Y\to J$. The hypotheses of [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] hold for $F=\ell$: it is additive by step 1, and K-injective resolutions in the tower category and their total-derived computation are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The cited computation represents $h$ by a homotopy class $g:I\to J$ with $Q_Tg=(Q_Tp)h(Q_Tq)^{-1}$ and gives
$$L(h)d_q=d_pQ_A(\ell g).$$
With the canonical localized shift identifications of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $g[r]$ represents $h[r]$ using $q[r],p[r]$, so the same formula gives $L(h[r])d_{q[r]}=d_{p[r]}Q_A(\ell(g[r]))$. Step 4 now gives
$$\beta_{Y,r}L(h[r])d_{q[r]}=d_p[r]\Lambda_{J,r}Q_A(\ell(g[r]))=d_p[r]Q_A(\ell g)[r]\Lambda_{I,r}=L(h)[r]\beta_{X,r}d_{q[r]}.$$
Cancel $d_{q[r]}$. This proves naturality for every derived morphism, including ones not represented by strict maps $X\to Y$.

source.place: Tags 070I (lemma-K-injective) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); explicit arbitrary-derived-morphism square using the existing general computation node.

proof.text:
For zero shift, choose $q[0]=q$ under the canonical identification. Step 4 and cancellation give $\beta_{X,0}=d_qd_q^{-1}=1$. For addition choose the resolutions $q$, $q[r]$, and $q[r][s]$ simultaneously. Substituting their formulas cancels the middle comparison:
$$\beta_{X,r}[s]\beta_{X[r],s}=d_q[r][s]\Lambda_{I,r}[s]\Lambda_{I[r],s}d_{q[r][s]}^{-1}.$$
The tuple identity in step 4 identifies the two middle maps with $\Lambda_{I,r+s}$, after the canonical addition-of-shifts isomorphisms. To check the remaining comparison under this reindexing, let $a_X:(X[r])[s]\to X[r+s]$ and $a_I:(I[r])[s]\to I[r+s]$ be the canonical chain isomorphisms. They satisfy $a_Iq[r][s]=q[r+s]a_X$. The morphism formula of step 6, applied to $Q_Ta_X$ and its representative $a_I$, gives
$$L(Q_Ta_X)d_{q[r][s]}=d_{q[r+s]}Q_A(\ell a_I).$$
Moreover $Q_A$ takes these chain reindexings to the prescribed shift associators [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently the preceding composite is precisely $\beta_{X,r+s}$ with the source and target addition-of-shifts identifications inserted. This proves coherence, also when $r$ or $s$ is negative. All comparison arguments used K-injectivity alone, not injectivity of individual degree terms.
